Scalable model diagnostic plots

Source: R/scalable-diagnostics.R
scalable_qq_plot.Rd

Aggregate all observations before drawing model diagnostic plots with ggplot. QQ points are grouped into bins of equal distance along the curve, keeping both endpoints. Heatmaps and histograms contain precomputed counts, so redrawing does not bin the original data again. Uniform references average draws as they are generated. Simulated references retain exact pooled quantiles, using temporary files above the configured memory threshold; see diagnostic_support.

Usage

scalable_qq_plot(
  model,
  method = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  n_uniform = 10,
  n_simulate = 50,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.9,
  qq_bins = 1000L,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  ci_col = "black",
  ci_alpha = 0.2,
  point_col = "grey20",
  point_alpha = 1,
  line_col = "red",
  by_family = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  ...,
  n_dharma = 250L
)

scalable_worm_plot(model, ..., n_dharma = 250L)

scalable_residuals_linpred_plot(
  model,
  type = NULL,
  density_bins = c(50L, 50L),
  density = c("conditional", "count"),
  seed = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  title = "Residuals vs linear predictor",
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  line_col = "red",
  by_family = NULL,
  rank = NULL,
  density_method = c("kde", "histogram"),
  bandwidth = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  ...,
  n_dharma = 250L
)

scalable_observed_fitted_plot(
  model,
  density_bins = c(50L, 50L),
  density = c("count", "conditional"),
  xlab = "Fitted values",
  ylab = "Response",
  title = "Observed vs fitted values",
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  by_family = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  ...
)

scalable_residuals_hist_plot(
  model,
  type = NULL,
  n_bins = c("sturges", "scott", "fd"),
  seed = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = "Frequency",
  title = "Histogram of residuals",
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  by_family = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  ...,
  n_dharma = 250L
)

Arguments

model

A fitted model supported by diagnostic_support.

method

character or NULL; how to calculate reference quantiles. Probability integral transform (PIT) and quantile residuals use fixed uniform and standard-normal references, respectively. For quantile residuals, "normal" also selects that fixed reference; other named methods require traditional residuals. For deviance, response and Pearson residuals:

  • "uniform" applies the fitted inverse cumulative distribution function (CDF) to randomised uniform quantiles and averages the resulting ordered residuals over n_uniform draws.

  • "simulate" generates n_simulate response data sets at the fitting covariates. Responses are generated together when needed to preserve dependence, and their ordered residuals supply reference values and bands.

  • "marginal" approximates the pooled distribution of individual residuals, without bands for dependence. This is selected for BAM GEE and PQL correlations that do not define a joint response distribution. Explicit joint simulation is unavailable in those cases.

  • "normal" uses a normal approximation fitted to the residual location and scale. For dependent responses it omits bands based on independence.

  • "direct" is deprecated in favour of "uniform".

For ordinary GAMs, NULL selects "simulate" for Tweedie and "uniform" otherwise. Missing inverse CDFs cause a switch to simulation; missing response generators can cause a switch to a normal approximation for independent responses. Dependent responses use joint simulation when available, or marginal checks otherwise. For grouped families, NULL selects simulation if every component has a generator, or inverse-CDF sampling with a message if every component has an inverse CDF. If neither is available, it gives an error; a normal approximation must be requested explicitly.

type

Residual type; NULL follows the model-specific defaults in appraise(). PIT and quantile residuals are available for supported response distributions. "surrogate" is available for ocat() and multinom() GAMs with method = NULL: logistic references for ordinal residuals and centred Gumbel references for each nominal category utility. Nominal components always have separate panels. Their residuals are drawn once per observation and shared with ordinary diagnostics. Components are summarised one at a time; QQ bin limits apply to each category. Residuals use category probabilities on the predictor axis, including category 0. See surrogate_residuals() and diagnostic_support.

n_uniform

numeric; number of inverse-CDF draws to average when method = "uniform".

n_simulate

numeric; number of data sets to simulate from the estimated model when using the simulation method (method = "simulate").

seed

Random seed for QQ calculations or randomized residuals. Explicit seeds preserve the caller's RNG state, including an absent state.

level

Coverage of pointwise QQ reference intervals, strictly between zero and one. Used by simulation and normal-reference methods.

qq_bins

Maximum number of QQ points per family component, including both endpoints; an integer of at least three.

xlab, ylab

Axis labels; NULL selects suitable defaults.

title, subtitle, caption

Plot title, subtitle and caption, passed to ggplot2::labs().

ci_col

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Fill colour for reference intervals, including bands for quantile residuals.

ci_alpha

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Alpha transparency for reference intervals.

point_col

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Constant point colour when family components are not mapped to colour. Pooled grouped diagnostics instead colour points by component.

point_alpha

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Alpha transparency of points on the QQ plot.

line_col

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Colour used to draw the reference line.

by_family

logical or NULL; separate indexed grouped-family components into facets. The default pools quantile residuals with component colours and facets traditional residuals. TRUE and FALSE explicitly select the layout. In appraise(), observed-versus-fitted values always use component facets. Standalone observed_fitted_plot() facets by default and permits explicit pooling. Ignored for ordinary models.

conditioning

character or NULL; "conditional" holds fitted random effects fixed, "marginal" averages over new effects, and "gam_component" uses the extracted GAM. Availability and defaults depend on the model; see diagnostic_support.

...

optional arguments used to prepare the model for diagnostics, including sdmTMB field_method. For scalable_worm_plot(), other arguments pass to scalable_qq_plot() except its internal worm setting.

n_dharma

positive integer; number of response simulations for type = "dharma". This is separate from n_simulate, which controls traditional QQ reference calculations. Defaults to 250.

density_bins

Positive integer or pair of integers giving the number of horizontal and vertical heatmap bins.

density

One of "conditional" or "count". Conditional density is estimated using density_method. With "histogram", it is the count divided by the horizontal-bin total and vertical-bin width. Empty horizontal bins are blank. Counts are always unsmoothed.

rank

logical or NULL; use within-component ranks on the horizontal axis of residual-versus-predictor plots. The default ranks pooled grouped plots and retains original predictors in facets. TRUE or FALSE overrides this independently of the residual type and layout. Only finite observations included in each component determine its ranks; average ties are used.

density_method

Conditional-density estimator: "kde" (the default) uses KernSmooth::bkde2D() with Gaussian kernels; "histogram" uses unsmoothed rectangular bins. Only affects the residual heatmap.

bandwidth

Optional pair of positive bandwidths for the predictor and residual axes, in their plotted units. NULL uses normal-reference bandwidths, adjusted for two dimensions, with a fallback for constant axes. Used only for density_method = "kde" and conditional density.

n_bins

character or numeric; either the number of bins or a string indicating how to calculate the number of bins.

Value

A ggplot object containing aggregated plotting data.

Details

GJRM support covers uncensored univariate N, LN, GA, GAi, P, NBI, and NBII models. PIT/quantile references are uniform/normal; traditional response/Pearson references use inverse-CDF or simulated responses. Probabilities are recomputed from final likelihood parameters. Quantile QQ bands give pointwise intervals for ordered standard-normal residuals, conditional on the fitted distribution, without accounting for parameter estimation. Observed-versus-fitted plots use response means, including the lognormal mean correction. Residuals are plotted against the first distributional linear predictor.

Grouped-family models retain the residual defaults, component reference distributions, predictor ranks and layout controls of appraise(). QQ bin limits apply separately to each component. Pooled residual heatmaps summarize the component mixture rather than colouring individual observations; observed-versus-fitted appraisals always separate components. Pooled histograms use faint component-coloured fills with opaque stepped upper boundaries, retaining common bin edges and component densities.

Residual-versus-predictor plots identify the response family in the subtitle and show conditioning and field choices in the caption where relevant, matching residuals_linpred_plot(). Supply caption = "" to omit the caption.

Kernel density estimates are calculated on a fixed grid before plotting. Each predictor slice is normalized to integrate to one over the displayed residual grid. Bandwidths, rather than density_bins, control smoothing; increase grid resolution when using small bandwidths. A square-root fill transformation reveals low-density regions while retaining density units in the legend. Gaussian kernels smooth the bands that discrete residuals can form even under a correctly specified count model. Smoothing does not give traditional residuals a common reference distribution.

Point styling affects QQ and worm points. Heatmap fill scales can be replaced with ggplot scales. Non-finite plotting observations are reported and omitted; fitting exclusions do not count as dropped observations.

References

Fasiolo, M., Nedellec, R., Goude, Y. and Wood, S. N. (2020). Scalable Visualization Methods for Modern Generalized Additive Models. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 29, 78-86. doi:10.1080/10618600.2019.1629942.

See also

appraise(), qq_plot(), worm_plot()

Examples

library("mgcv")
dat <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, seed = 2)
m <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = dat)
scalable_qq_plot(m, seed = 42)

scalable_residuals_linpred_plot(m)

scalable_observed_fitted_plot(m, density_bins = c(30, 40))

appraise(m, scalable = TRUE, seed = 42)
